title: Read One Line: x-t Graphs Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
A runner, a bus, a cycle to college: one picture can tell the whole story of each trip. Aarav's cycle app shows just one line. Where did he stop? Where was he fastest? Did he ever turn back? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 2, Motion in a Straight Line) we learn to read position-time graphs.

A live motion notebook runs Aarav's ride with a readout and an x-t graph that draws as he moves: steady, stopped at a signal, then faster, with a slow-motion replay. We show step by step why the slope of an x-t graph is the velocity, compare lines going up and down, and use tangents on a curve to find the velocity at an instant. Then a worked example, the exam trap about graphs and paths, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 One line on a cycle app
0:28 What is a position-time graph?
0:50 Live sim: steady, stopped, faster
1:27 Slope = velocity, step by step
2:07 Line going up vs going down + pause and think
2:43 Curves and tangents: Aarav's ride from home
3:33 Worked example: velocity from two points
4:00 Exam trap: the graph is not the road
4:25 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:06 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Velocity-Time Graphs. What if we plot velocity instead of position? The area under that line hides the distance.
